Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the demo: 

Summary notes:
- Integration scope: server-side API calls from your orchestration layer to Redwood (inference + embeddings/rerankers).
- Auth options discussed: API keys (simple, Redwood-managed), OAuth/JWT service-account flow (recommended for long-lived service accounts + rotation), and customer-signed JWTs (supported).
- Key management concerns: rotation cadence, RBAC for keys, audit logging, KMS integration for private key material.
- Routing & structured output: you want per-tenant routing and structured tool-calling support (JSON schema enforcement).

Action items / asks for FintechCo:
1) Which auth model do you prefer for production? (API keys vs service account JWT vs OAuth)
2) Who on your infra/security team should we loop in for KMS/rotation details?
3) Any constraints on header/circuit-breaker vs request-level timeouts we should account for?

Attached: FintechCo-MAP-v1.2.pdf (mutual action plan) and Redwood-API-Key-Rotation-Guide.pdf — the guide has examples for service accounts, JWT signing, and recommended rotation patterns.

Next steps proposed:
- If you prefer service accounts/JWT, we can provide a small PoC SDK snippet and an example rotation webhook flow for your Key Management system.
- Schedule a follow-up with your security lead next week to confirm KMS options and rotation SLA.

Can you confirm preferred auth model and who we should invite for the security call?

Marissa, 

Appreciate the recap — that aligns with our notes. A few answers and follow-ups from our side:

1) Preference: leaning toward a service-account JWT model so we can centrally manage keys in our KMS and grant least-privilege to the token issuer. API keys are OK for short-term testing but not for prod.
2) Security lead: looping in Priya (cc'd) — she handles infra security and KMS. Priya, we'd like to confirm whether Redwood supports verifying JWTs signed by our customer KMS (we'd prefer SRS-based keys rather than Redwood holding private keys).
3) Rotation cadence: we'd aim for 30-90 day rotation for signing keys; want to avoid service disruption during rollover.

Questions: 
- Do you support JWKS endpoint fetching in your token validation flow, or do we need to push public keys to Redwood manually during onboarding?
- For short-lived bearer tokens (issued by our token service), do you offer a token-introspection / revocation API or do you rely on signature+exp checks?

We can set a 30-min sync with Priya and your engineering lead to walk through the technical flow. Available Thu 11–1 ET or Fri 9–11 ET.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Integrations | FintechCo

Alex / Priya,

Thanks for the clarification — short technical answers below plus a suggested PoC approach. Happy to jump on the call you suggested.

High-level support from Redwood:
- JWKS: Redwood supports automated JWKS discovery. You can point us at a stable jwks_uri and we will fetch/refresh keys; we also accept manual upload of public keys during onboarding if you prefer.
- JWT validation: We validate signature + exp + nbf + optional custom claims (aud, tid). You can configure required claims per tenant.
- Short-lived bearer tokens: We validate signatures and expiry; we do not currently call an external token-introspection endpoint by default (performance reasons), but we support optional revocation checks via a webhook (your token service can call us to mark tokens revoked) or we can implement introspection for specific tenants in the PoC.
- Service accounts: Our SDKs include a lightweight token adapter that can request short-lived tokens (if you prefer) or accept externally-issued JWTs. For fully customer-managed keys, we do not need to hold private keys — we only need your JWKS or public key thumbprints.

Recommended rotation/rollover pattern (safe, non-disruptive):
1) Publish new key to your JWKS with a new kid and overlap both keys for a 24–48 hour window.
2) Redwood will fetch and accept both keys during overlap.
3) After traffic has shifted and no tokens are issued with the old key, you can remove the old key from JWKS.

Example header + curl: 
- Authorization: Bearer <JWT>
- Example validation: signature (RS256), exp checked, aud = "redwood-inference"

cURL sample (using customer-signed JWT):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_JWT>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-1","input":"summarize..."}'

PoC suggestion:
- Phase 1 (2 days): short test using customer-signed JWTs + JWKS discovery against a staging jwks_uri. We validate signature/claims and return sample embeddings/reranker calls.
- Phase 2 (1 day): add rotation test with overlapping keys and confirm no request failures during rollover.

We can also provide a tiny SDK snippet in Node/Python during the call. If you confirm Thu 11am ET we will share a calendar invite with a dial-in and include a brief agenda: JWKS discovery, sample JWT exchange, rotation test plan.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Engineer, Integrations | Redwood Inference
